summary: Alert indicates repeated SSH authentication failures from source IP 192.168.1.50 targeting user 'admin' on host Ubuntu-Server.
hypotheses: The source IP is attempting a brute-force attack against the admin account.
The failures may be from legitimate user mistyping credentials.
The failures could be due to an automated reconnaissance tool scanning for valid credentials.
investigation_steps: Review /var/log/auth.log for the number and timing of SSH authentication attempts from 192.168.1.50.
Check if the admin account is locked or disabled after repeated failures.
Determine if the source IP is associated with known malicious activity (e.g., via threat intelligence feeds).
Consider temporarily blocking or rate-limiting 192.168.1.50 on the SSH service.
Verify that no successful login has occurred from this IP.
Correlate with other logs (e.g., firewall, IDS) to identify additional malicious activity.
missing_information: Exact number of authentication attempts and timestamps.
Duration between attempts to confirm brute-force pattern.
Whether a successful login was achieved later.
Context on whether the admin account is commonly used or has elevated privileges.
